domain: A2 security of the shipped and private builds (net/, settings and caches, resource loading, web bridge and URL hooks, OS calls, CI and publishing)

risks.title: A connected LAN peer can freeze or exhaust memory on the other PC with one crafted packet
risks.player_impact: In the private LAN build the game on Orb's or Orb 2's PC hangs or runs out of memory; no code execution is possible.
risks.evidence: The peer's hello 'delay' is never capped (handshake.gd:84, :93) and NetSession._init loops range(delay) filling dicts (session.gd:128-129). Kind-2 Variant packets skip the binary layout's 255 caps and reach NetHost._take, where an integer 'inputs' makes 'for p in ...' run that many addInput calls (host.gd:126) and an unchecked takeover slot can hand any fighter, the victim's included, to the AI (host.gd:120-121).
risks.needs_outside_expert: No for the LAN test; a networking security review before any online mode ships.

risks.title: LAN link is unauthenticated and unencrypted; first device on the /24 takes the seat
risks.player_impact: Another device on the home network that connects first can join or disrupt the match; traffic is readable on the LAN.
risks.evidence: Plain ENet with no DTLS setup; the listener accepts the first peer whose address starts with the host's /24 prefix, and the match key is built from public seed, setup and data hash. Godot's ENetConnection offers dtls_server_setup, which is unused.
risks.needs_outside_expert: No for a home LAN test; yes before internet play.

risks.title: LAN kit's firewall rule applies on every network profile and persists until removed
risks.player_impact: On another network with the same common subnet (for example 10.0.0.x) the host PC still admits inbound UDP 47100 to the game while hosting.
risks.evidence: netsh rule uses profile=any with remoteip set to the /24 and stays until the removal script is run; the scripts self-elevate with ExecutionPolicy Bypass. The bind to one fixed IP (lan.gd:218) limits exposure.

risks.title: Live public web build packs 259 test and tool files it does not need
risks.player_impact: No direct player harm found; the public pck carries debug routes and process-spawning test scripts, a larger surface than needed.
risks.evidence: I parsed the live pck's file table (build_info says commit 257a766): it holds render/tools/flash_capture, render/anim/tools/*_study scenes and sim/core/tools/batch, because the pinned preset excluded only prototype, qa, research, docs, tools and .github. At that commit, study and flashcap are dropped on a non-local host and lock_reduce_flashing is true, so the routes stay closed.

risks.title: Committed Web preset does not exclude net/ and has no network-class guard like the desktop packager
risks.player_impact: If the site pin moves past net/'s arrival, the public web pck will carry the LAN code as dead weight, contradicting any no-network claim.
risks.evidence: Desktop presets exclude net/* and desktop-package.mjs refuses network classes, but the Web preset (line 11) also omits render/tools/*. Nothing outside net/ references Net* classes, and Godot's web export has no low-level networking, so the code would be unreachable.

risks.title: Public play page can be framed (no anti-framing), so the HTML flashing gate could be clickjacked
risks.player_impact: A hostile site could frame /play/ and trick a visitor into clicking 'I understand, start' without seeing the flashing warning.
risks.evidence: curl -I shows no X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors (only Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *), and the gate is a page overlay with a start button. GitHub Pages cannot set headers; a frame-busting check in the page would be needed.

risks.title: A home LAN address is committed to the public repo
risks.player_impact: Reveals a private (non-routable) home-network address; no practical attack found.
risks.evidence: 10.0.0.135 appears in comments and a test; it is an RFC 1918 address. A pattern scan found no keys or tokens in the committed tree.

checked_ok.why: Only bytes_to_var is used, which Godot documents as not decoding objects. No bytes_to_var_with_objects, str_to_var, JSON.to_native or Expression appears in shipped code.
Counts are u8 and available bytes are checked before each read; the tail length is validated, so malformed packets return null.
The host binds the kit's own private IP (not all interfaces) with one peer slot and a /24 filter, and drops packets from non-peers before decoding.

checked_ok.where: grep for PacketPeerUDP, UDPServer, set_broadcast in all .gd; net/lan.gd:215-218
checked_ok.why: No broadcast or discovery responder exists; the joiner dials a fixed address.

checked_ok.area: Net code absent from public builds
checked_ok.where: export_presets.cfg:55,101,132; live pck file table; git ls-tree 257a766c net/ (0 files); net/tools/lan_kit.mjs:24,43-56,88-97
checked_ok.why: Desktop presets exclude net/*; the live web pck has no net/ entries; NetLan is wired in only by the kit patching a scratch copy, and nothing outside net/ references Net* classes.
It is fed in-process by the loopback relay; there is no socket path.
They use JSON.parse_string with a Dictionary type check, and Godot JSON yields no objects. A crafted local file can at worst cause script errors in remap.apply_file (remap.gd:435-443).
Magic, key text, length and SHA-256 are checked before use, and the payload goes through bytes_to_var with no objects.
The game loads no replay files. Every load() and scene change uses res:// data, and the study route needs a valid identifier under res://render/anim/tools and is local-only.
On a public host only skyreact, panhaze, nopanhaze and keyhelp survive; study, flashcap and debug words are dropped by a hostname check, and the live pinned build gates them the same way.

Evaluated text is constant or JSON.stringify-escaped engine and data values; no page or URL text is evaluated. The capture hook (window.__flashcap) attaches only on a local host or a capture_hook build.

checked_ok.where: ui/widgets/ui_feedback.gd:264-288; ui/data/send.json _target none; grep for HTTPRequest, OS.execute, create_process
checked_ok.why: shell_open gets only the data-defined feedback URL with uri_encoded user text, and the send target is none. OS.execute and create_process appear only in tool scripts, and there is no HTTPRequest, HTTPClient or WebSocket in shipped code.
Read-only token by default, actions pinned by SHA, persist-credentials false, deploy only on main and not for pull requests; Godot, the templates and the custom web template are checked by SHA-512.
The only public release and artifact is the web template; no desktop or LAN build is published, and desktop artifacts keep for one day.
/band/ and /bench/ serve the holding page, so no prototype build is exposed.
There are no autoloads; the main scene is boot_entry.

limits: I did not run Godot, so the hang paths and how a release export behaves after a GDScript runtime error are traced, not reproduced.

I could not confirm Godot 4.7.2's bytes_to_var recursion cap or ENet maximum packet size; the depth check I saw is in a master-branch source mirror (cocalc.com/github/godotengine/godot/blob/master/core/io/marshalls.cpp).
I inspected the live site through curl of its pages, the pck file table and two small data files in it; the custom index.wasm was not examined.
The LAN folders actually given to Orb and Orb 2 are not in the repo; I judged them from net/tools/lan_kit.mjs, and a kept-build tree may differ.
Per the independence rule I did not read docs/legal, docs/net, docs/qa, docs/ep or audit/, so Legal rows that code comments cite are unverified.
